properties.summary: Photoluminescence is slightly blue-shifted relative to CeBr3, whose maximum emission is 371 nm under the reported comparison.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: Two eight-coordinate Ce(III) square antiprisms share a bromide-containing edge to form an isolated dimer; four methanol oxygen atoms complete each Ce coordination sphere. The dimers pack through hydrogen bonding.

synthesis.procedure: In an argon glovebox, approximately 0.5 g of CeBr3 was placed in a round-bottom flask and sealed with a septum. After removal from the glovebox, approximately 10 mL of anhydrous methanol was added by syringe to form a supersaturated solution with some undissolved solid. The solution was syringe-filtered into a purged glass vessel and allowed to evaporate slowly under nitrogen while excluding water.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: Septum-sealed round-bottom flask; slow evaporation in a purged glass vessel
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Syringe filtration followed by slow evaporation under nitrogen

properties.summary: Photoluminescence is blue-shifted relative to CeBr3, whose maximum emission is 371 nm under the reported comparison. Scintillation of compound 2 was proposed for future investigation, not demonstrated here.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: An isolated dimer of edge-sharing, eight-coordinate Ce(III) square antiprisms analogous to compound 1, with ethanol rather than methanol ligands. Hydrogen bonding connects the molecular dimers in the crystal packing.

synthesis.procedure: Prepared by the explicit slow-evaporation method described for compound 1, substituting anhydrous ethanol for methanol: approximately 0.5 g of CeBr3 was handled in an argon glovebox, solvent was added to make a supersaturated solution, and the filtered solution was slowly evaporated under nitrogen. The article notes inadvertent introduction of a small amount of water during preparations including compound 2; no amount is specified.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: A discrete tetramer has two distinct eight-coordinate Ce(III) environments. Each hydroxide bridges three Ce centers, with additional bromide bridges completing the tetramer. The tetrameric units are held together in the crystal through intermolecular hydrogen bonding.

synthesis.procedure: Prepared by the explicit shared slow-evaporation procedure using approximately 0.5 g of CeBr3 and anhydrous 2-propanol, with handling under argon, syringe filtration and slow evaporation under nitrogen. Water was inadvertently incorporated. The authors attribute incorporated hydroxide to possible KOH residue from washing the glassware in a base bath; KOH was not reported as a deliberately measured addition.
